name: SiYuan
tagline: A local-first notebook with blocks, backlinks and databases
description: A personal knowledge app that keeps everything on your own device: block-based documents, links between any two blocks, and databases with table and board views inside ordinary pages. It runs as a desktop and mobile app, or as a single container with a web interface.
licenseNote: The app is AGPL-3.0 and free to use. Syncing between devices is a paid feature, whether through the developers' cloud or your own S3 or WebDAV storage, and the developers advise against syncing its folder with other tools. Check current terms before depending on sync.
backing: B3log, a small company in China, funded by subscriptions and one-off purchases

maturity.rationale: Released very frequently for years and widely used. A small team, a fast release pace and data kept in its own format mean you should keep exports of anything important.

strengths: Databases with table and board views sit inside ordinary documents, as in Notion
Works fully offline; nothing leaves your device unless you turn sync on
Links and embeds work at the level of a single block
Apps for every desktop and mobile platform, plus a container with a web interface
weaknesses: A personal tool: no shared workspace, permissions or real-time editing with colleagues
Sync between devices costs money, even to your own storage
Notes are kept in its own JSON format rather than Markdown, though it exports Markdown
The interface and documentation are translated from Chinese and uneven in places

featureNotes.plain-files: Its own JSON files in a local folder; exports to Markdown
featureNotes.public-sharing: Read-only publishing from a running instance
featureNotes.notion-import: Via Notion's Markdown export; databases arrive as plain tables
